title: Where did God come from?
shortAnswer: God did not come from anywhere. He is uncreated and eternal — the one being who simply is, from whom everything else derives its existence.

title: If God is good, why is there evil and suffering?
shortAnswer: Scripture does not explain evil away; it says God is neither its author nor its victim, and that in Christ he entered suffering rather than merely permitting it.

title: How can God be three Persons and one God?
shortAnswer: One divine essence subsisting in three distinct Persons — not three gods, not one Person in three masks. The distinction is of relation, not of substance.

title: Did God create sin?
shortAnswer: God created beings capable of choosing, and that capacity was good. Sin arose from the misuse of that freedom, not from a defect in what God made.

title: Why did God allow Satan to exist?
shortAnswer: Satan is a creature, not a rival deity. His existence is permitted within strict limits, and his defeat is already accomplished at the cross.

title: Is God's sovereignty compatible with human free will?
shortAnswer: Scripture asserts both without resolving the mechanism: God works genuinely, and human choices are genuinely ours and genuinely accountable.

title: What does it mean that Jesus is fully God and fully man?
shortAnswer: One Person in two complete natures, divine and human, united without confusion, change, division or separation — the Chalcedonian definition of AD 451.

title: Did Jesus have to die, or was there another way?
shortAnswer: The New Testament treats the cross as necessary given God's justice and mercy together — Gethsemane's 'if it be possible' received no alternative.

title: Is faith alone enough for salvation?
shortAnswer: All traditions agree salvation is by grace and that saving faith is never barren. They differ on whether works are the fruit of justification or part of its ground.

title: Can a saved person lose salvation?
shortAnswer: Scripture holds together strong promises of preservation and severe warnings against falling away; every tradition must account for both sets of texts.

title: What happens to those who never heard the gospel?
shortAnswer: Scripture insists God is just and that Christ is the only Saviour, while leaving the fate of the unevangelised largely to God's judgment rather than to our formula.

title: Is hell eternal conscious torment?
shortAnswer: All traditions affirm a real and final judgment. The debate is over the nature and duration of the punishment, not over whether judgment is real.

title: Does purgatory exist?
shortAnswer: The question is whether the saved undergo a purifying process after death. All agree that nothing unclean enters God's presence; they differ on how that cleansing occurs.

title: Should we pray to Mary and the saints?
shortAnswer: Everyone agrees Christ is the sole Mediator of redemption. The dispute is whether asking a departed saint to pray for us is intercession within the Body or a rival mediation.

title: Was Mary sinless and ever-virgin?
shortAnswer: All Christians honour Mary as Theotokos, mother of the Lord. Traditions divide on the Immaculate Conception and on whether she bore other children.

title: Is baptism necessary for salvation?
shortAnswer: Baptism is universally commanded and never treated as optional. The division is whether it conveys regeneration or signifies a regeneration already received.

title: Should infants be baptized?
shortAnswer: The dispute turns on whether the covenant sign belongs to households as circumcision did, or only to those who personally profess faith.

title: What actually happens in Holy Communion?
shortAnswer: Every tradition treats the Supper as the central act of Christian worship and as a real encounter with Christ; they differ on the mode of his presence.

title: Is the Bible alone sufficient, or do we need tradition?
shortAnswer: All sides use Scripture and all sides read it within a community. The question is whether tradition is a second source or the Church's servant reading of the one source.

title: Which books belong in the Bible, and who decided?
shortAnswer: The canon was recognised rather than invented, over centuries, on grounds of apostolicity, orthodoxy and universal use. Its Old Testament boundary is still disputed.

title: Are the gifts of tongues, prophecy and healing for today?
shortAnswer: The question is whether the miraculous gifts ceased with the apostolic age or continue. All agree the Spirit remains active; they differ on the form of that activity.

title: Is speaking in tongues the evidence of the Holy Spirit?
shortAnswer: All agree the Spirit indwells every believer. The dispute is whether tongues is the necessary sign of a distinct post-conversion baptism in the Spirit.

title: Can women be pastors, priests or preachers?
shortAnswer: All agree women share fully in salvation and in gifting for ministry. The dispute concerns the office of ordained governing and teaching authority.

title: Is divorce and remarriage ever permitted?
shortAnswer: All hold marriage to be a lifelong covenant and divorce a grievous evil. They differ on whether any exception permits remarriage while the spouse lives.

title: What does the Bible say about homosexuality?
shortAnswer: The historic Christian teaching restricts sexual union to marriage between a man and a woman, while insisting on the equal dignity of every person and rejecting contempt or cruelty.

title: Is the Sabbath Saturday or Sunday?
shortAnswer: Christians gathered on the first day from the earliest records, marking the resurrection. Whether that transfers the fourth commandment or fulfils it is the point at issue.

title: Should Christians tithe ten percent?
shortAnswer: Generous, sacrificial and regular giving is commanded everywhere in the New Testament; whether the specific ten percent figure carries over from the Law is disputed.

title: Is it wrong to use images or icons in worship?
shortAnswer: All reject the worship of any created thing. The dispute is whether veneration passing through an image to its prototype is idolatry or legitimate honour.

title: Do Christians still have to keep the Old Testament law?
shortAnswer: The moral character of God's law abides while the ceremonial and civil order given to Israel finds its fulfilment in Christ.

title: What is the unforgivable sin?
shortAnswer: In context it is the deliberate attribution of the Spirit's evident work to Satan — a settled and knowing rejection, not a fearful doubt.

title: Can Christians be demon-possessed?
shortAnswer: All affirm the reality of the demonic and the greater power of Christ. The debate is whether a believer indwelt by the Spirit can be possessed, as against oppressed or harassed.

title: Does God still speak outside the Bible?
shortAnswer: Christ is God's final and sufficient word. Whether God gives further non-canonical guidance — and how it is tested — divides the traditions.

title: Is predestination fair?
shortAnswer: Election is taught plainly in Scripture and so is God's genuine desire that none perish. Every system must hold both, and each does so differently.

title: How do we reconcile Genesis with modern science?
shortAnswer: Genesis answers who and why rather than the mechanism and rate. Christians divide over the genre and chronology of the days while agreeing God is the sole Creator.

title: Was Adam a real historical person?
shortAnswer: Paul's argument in Romans 5 and 1 Corinthians 15 parallels Adam with Christ, which is why the historicity question carries doctrinal weight rather than merely historical interest.

title: Is suicide an unforgivable sin?
shortAnswer: The historic instinct that suicide forecloses repentance has been tempered by understanding of mental illness and by the recognition that no sin outruns the cross.

title: Is abortion always wrong?
shortAnswer: The Christian tradition has consistently opposed abortion from the earliest centuries, while differing on hard cases where the mother's life is directly threatened.

title: Can Christians serve in war or take a life?
shortAnswer: The Church has produced both a robust just-war tradition and a continuous pacifist witness; both claim the Sermon on the Mount.

title: How should Christians relate to government?
shortAnswer: Submission to lawful authority is commanded, and so is refusal when the state commands what God forbids — 'we must obey God rather than men.'

title: Is wealth a blessing or a danger?
shortAnswer: Scripture treats possessions as a stewardship and a spiritual hazard at once. It never condemns wealth as such, and never leaves it unexamined.

title: What is the church — building, denomination, or people?
shortAnswer: The Church is the people of God, the body of Christ, and the temple of the Spirit — never merely an institution or a venue, though it takes visible form.

title: Is there salvation outside the church?
shortAnswer: The ancient maxim extra ecclesiam nulla salus is affirmed in some sense by all, but the definition of 'church' does the decisive work.

title: What is the purpose of suffering for a believer?
shortAnswer: Suffering is never called good in itself, but God is repeatedly shown using it to form character, deepen dependence and conform believers to Christ.

title: Does God heal today, and why are some not healed?
shortAnswer: All traditions pray for the sick and confess that God heals. None can guarantee the timing, and Scripture itself records unhealed servants of God.

title: What is the baptism in the Holy Spirit?
shortAnswer: Every believer receives the Spirit at conversion. Whether there is a distinct subsequent empowering, and what marks it, is the dividing question.

title: Is the rapture biblical, and when does it occur?
shortAnswer: All Christians confess Christ will return bodily and gather his people. Whether that gathering is a separate event before a tribulation is a modern and contested question.

title: Who is the Antichrist?
shortAnswer: John uses the term for any spirit denying that Jesus is the Christ come in flesh; Paul speaks of a coming man of sin. Both a present spirit and a final figure are in view.

title: Will there be a literal new earth?
shortAnswer: The Christian hope is not escape from matter but the renewal of it — a resurrected body on a restored earth, not disembodied souls in a distant sky.

title: Are other religions entirely false?
shortAnswer: Christianity claims Christ as uniquely and universally the Saviour, which does not require denying every true or good thing found elsewhere.

title: How can we trust the Bible when manuscripts differ?
shortAnswer: The differences are overwhelmingly minor spelling variations, word order, and obvious scribal slips. No Christian doctrine rests on a contested reading.

title: What is the meaning of the Trinity's perichoresis or circumincession?
shortAnswer: The mutual indwelling and interpenetration of the three divine Persons without confusion of their distinct hypostases.

title: How does Christian theology understand divine impassibility?
shortAnswer: God is not subject to involuntary passions or emotional turbulence caused by external agents, yet possesses perfect, active love and compassion.

title: What is the biblical basis for creatio ex nihilo (creation out of nothing)?
shortAnswer: God brought the universe into existence without preexisting matter or eternal chaos, establishing absolute transcendence.

title: What does Scripture teach regarding the imago Dei in fallen humanity?
shortAnswer: The image of God is defaced and corrupted by the Fall but not eradicated, remaining the ground of universal human dignity.

title: How do the covenants of works and grace relate in covenant theology?
shortAnswer: Adam failed the probation of the covenant of works; Christ as the second Adam fulfilled all righteousness in the covenant of grace.

title: What is the difference between active and passive obedience of Christ?
shortAnswer: Active obedience is Christ's lifelong fulfillment of the moral law; passive obedience is his willing submission to the penal curse of death.

title: What is the theological distinction between propitiation and expiation?
shortAnswer: Propitiation placates the holy wrath of God; expiation covers and removes the defilement and guilt of sin.

title: What is the hypostatic union defined at Chalcedon (AD 451)?
shortAnswer: Two distinct, unconfused, unchanged, indivisible, and inseparable natures (divine and human) united in the single Person of the Son.

title: Did Jesus have one human will or two wills (divine and human)?
shortAnswer: The Sixth Ecumenical Council (Constantinople III, 681) affirmed dyothelitism: Christ has two wills and two operations, human and divine in harmony.

title: What is the significance of Christ's descent into Hades/Sheol?
shortAnswer: Christ proclaimed triumph over demonic powers and liberated the righteous souls awaiting redemption, inaugurating the defeat of death.

title: What is the nature of the resurrection body described in 1 Corinthians 15?
shortAnswer: A real, physical, yet glorified and immortal somatic body animated and transformed by the Holy Spirit (soma pneumatikon).

title: What is the session of Christ at the right hand of the Father?
shortAnswer: Christ's supreme exaltation, cosmic enthronement, and ongoing heavenly intercession as High Priest and King.

title: What is the filioque clause and why did it divide East and West?
shortAnswer: The Western insertion of 'and the Son' in the Creed; East defended the monarchia of the Father, West emphasized the co-equality of Son and Spirit.

title: What is regeneration and how does it precede saving faith in Reformed thought?
shortAnswer: The supernatural, monergistic awakening of the dead soul by the Spirit, enabling belief; other traditions hold faith and new birth occur simultaneously.

title: What is the difference between imputed and infused righteousness?
shortAnswer: Imputed righteousness is credited forensically to the believer's legal standing; infused righteousness is poured inward through sacraments.

title: What is the doctrine of the perspicuity (clarity) of Scripture?
shortAnswer: The core truths necessary for salvation are so clearly presented in Scripture that anyone reading with ordinary discernment can understand them.

title: What is the analogia fidei (analogy of faith) in hermeneutics?
shortAnswer: The principle that obscure or difficult biblical texts must be interpreted in light of the clear, overarching teaching of the entire biblical canon.

title: What is progressive revelation across redemptive history?
shortAnswer: God revealed his plan, character, and covenant gradually over centuries, culminating fully and decisively in Jesus Christ.

title: How does typology differ from allegory in biblical interpretation?
shortAnswer: Typology discovers real historical persons and events intended by God as prophetic shadows of Christ; allegory searches for hidden philosophical senses.

title: What are the four senses of scripture in classical Christian exegetical tradition?
shortAnswer: The medieval Quadriga: literal (historical event), allegorical (what to believe), tropological/moral (what to do), and anagogical (what to hope for).

title: What is the regulative principle versus the normative principle of worship?
shortAnswer: Regulative principle allows only what Scripture expressly commands; normative principle permits whatever Scripture does not forbid.

title: What is the communion of saints (communio sanctorum)?
shortAnswer: The spiritual solidarity and fellowship binding all believers in heaven and on earth together in the one mystical body of Christ.

title: What is the difference between the visible and invisible Church?
shortAnswer: The visible Church is the historical professing congregation; the invisible Church is the elect company known infallibly to God alone.

title: What constitutes the valid administration of Christian baptism?
shortAnswer: Water applied in the threefold Trinitarian name by an authorized minister with the intention to do what the Church does.

title: How do Christian traditions interpret the real presence in the Eucharist?
shortAnswer: Transubstantiation (Catholic), sacramental union (Lutheran), spiritual real presence by faith (Reformed), and memorial feast (Zwinglian).

title: What is the sacramental seal and indelible character of baptism and ordination?
shortAnswer: A permanent spiritual mark imprinted on the soul by certain sacraments that cannot be repeated or erased.

title: What is the biblical teaching on Christian stewardship and financial giving?
shortAnswer: Cheerful, proportional, sacrificial giving for gospel proclamation, local church sustenance, and relief of the impoverished.

title: What is the theological basis for Christian fasting?
shortAnswer: Fasting disciplines the flesh, intensifies prayer, fosters solidarity with the poor, and expresses hunger for the kingdom of God.

title: How should Christians understand the role of civil disobedience?
shortAnswer: Civil authorities possess God-given jurisdiction for justice, but when human decrees contradict divine commandments, obedience to God is mandatory.

title: What is the biblical view of the intermediate state between death and resurrection?
shortAnswer: Believers enter conscious, joyful rest in Christ's presence; unbelievers await final judgment; bodily resurrection occurs at Christ's return.

title: How does amillennialism interpret Revelation 20's thousand-year reign?
shortAnswer: The millennium is the current church age between Christ's first and second comings, where Satan is bound from deceiving the nations wholesale.

title: How does historic premillennialism interpret the return of Christ?
shortAnswer: Christ returns visibly and bodily before inaugurating a literal earthly millennium prior to the final judgment and new creation.

title: How does postmillennialism understand the progress of the gospel?
shortAnswer: The preaching of the gospel and work of the Spirit will gradually Christianize the nations before Christ returns to a largely converted world.

title: What is the biblical nature of the final judgment?
shortAnswer: A public, universal, righteous evaluation by Jesus Christ where all secrets are revealed, rewards bestowed, and condemnation executed.

title: What is the New Jerusalem and its cubic dimensions in Revelation 21?
shortAnswer: The consummate city-temple dwelling of God with humanity, shaped as a cube to reflect the Holy of Holies where God's presence fills all in all.

title: What is the doctrine of common grace and how does it sustain human society?
shortAnswer: God's unmerited goodness restraining sin and bestowing civic order, science, and beauty upon all mankind without saving them.

title: What is prevenient grace in Wesleyan-Arminian theology?
shortAnswer: Universal grace preceding salvation that restores the fallen human will to a state where it is genuinely able to accept or resist the gospel.

title: What is the Reformed understanding of irresistible (effectual) grace?
shortAnswer: The internal call of the Spirit that infallibly overcomes human resistance in the elect, renewing their heart to desire Christ freely.

title: What is the doctrine of total depravity (or radical corruption)?
shortAnswer: Sin infects every faculty of the human person (mind, will, affection) such that fallen humanity cannot seek or please God apart from grace.

title: What is unconditional election in classical theology?
shortAnswer: God's eternal choice of certain sinners unto salvation grounded solely in his sovereign grace and pleasure, not foreseen human merit.

title: What is the debate surrounding definite (particular) atonement?
shortAnswer: Whether Christ died with the specific design to effectually redeem the elect (particular), or to make salvation possible for all (universal).

title: What is the perseverance of the saints versus conditional security?
shortAnswer: Whether true believers are preserved eternally by God's power, or can apostatize through persistent unbelief and forfeit salvation.

title: What is the role of natural law in Christian ethical deliberation?
shortAnswer: The moral order woven by the Creator into creation and human conscience, accessible to human reason though confirmed by special revelation.

title: What is Christian theodicy in the face of natural disasters (physical evil)?
shortAnswer: Physical evils stem from the curse on creation and the fallen world order, serving as sober reminders of human fragility and the need for repentance.

title: What is the biblical basis for church discipline and restoration?
shortAnswer: A loving, structured pastoral process to correct sin, preserve the purity and witness of the church, and restore the fallen brother.

title: What is the difference between ministerial and magisterial authority?
shortAnswer: Magisterial authority enacts laws on its own right; ministerial authority simply declares and administers the revealed laws of Christ the King.

title: How does the Bible address slavery across historical contexts?
shortAnswer: Scripture regulated ancient Near Eastern bondservanthood and planted spiritual principles of universal equality in Christ that dismantled institutional slavery.

title: What is the biblical definition of marriage?
shortAnswer: A lifelong, public, covenantal union of one man and one woman established by God at creation and reflecting the mystery of Christ and the Church.

title: What is the biblical balance between Christian liberty and stumbling blocks?
shortAnswer: Believers are free in matters indifferent (adiaphora), but must voluntarily curtail their liberties out of love to avoid causing weaker brethren to stumble.

title: What is the ultimate purpose of human existence (telos)?
shortAnswer: To glorify God, delight in his presence, and enjoy communion with him forever in the new creation.
